newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish board plays down report on Astra.
newsitem.headline: Swedish board plays down report on Astra.

text.p: Sweden's pharmaceutical control board played down the significance of a newspaper report about an alleged skin reaction in an elderly patient treated with Astra's Losec ulcer medicine.
The board confirmed it had written to the country's doctors mentioning the case.

"It was a thoroughly routine publication. We did not raise our eyebrows especially over this case. We wanted to remind the doctors to pay attention to cases like this," Orjan Mortimer, a doctor at the control board, told Reuters.
The mass-circulation newspaper Expressen reported earlier that the patient in question had contracted a rare skin disease called Lyells syndrome.
The paper quoted Astra spokesman Staffan Ternby as excluding any connection between Losec and the skin disease.
Mortimer said: "One can contract (Lyells) for other reasons, for example infections but also for reasons which we cannot identify."
He declined to say whether the board was corresponding with Astra about the case.
Astra's Ternby could not be reached for comment on the newspaper and board reports.
